text: Where does a payment system start, if not with payments?
prefix: Where does a payment system start, if not with payments?

text: With a stack, a build, and an environment that runs with one command.
prefix: With a stack, a build, and an environment that runs with one command.

text: We chose Java twenty-five and Spring Boot four: long-term support, and the most widely used stack for Java services.
prefix: We chose Java twenty-five and Spring Boot four: long-term support, and the most widely used stack for Java services.

text: We chose Gradle, with builds in Groovy, because the build is the pipeline: it generates code from the contracts, checks the style, and runs the tests, the same way on every machine.
prefix: We chose Gradle, with builds in Groovy, because the build is the pipeline: it generates code from the contracts, checks the style, and runs the tests, the same way on every machine.

text: The app is one modular monolith with six modules, partner, commission, e POS, BIN, card, and payment: one deploy today, and clean seams for tomorrow.
prefix: The app is one modular monolith with six modules, partner, commission, e POS, BIN, card, and payment: one deploy today, and clean seams for tomorrow.

text: Each module owns its own schema in one database, and connects as its own user, which can see that schema and nothing else.
prefix: Each module owns its own schema in one database, and connects as its own user, which can see that schema and nothing else.

text: A module asks another only through that module's contract, the internal operations in its OpenAPI file, and the build fails if it reaches any further.
prefix: A module asks another only through that module's contract, the internal operations in its OpenAPI file, and the build fails if it reaches any further.

text: Inside, every module uses the one layout every Spring developer knows: layered, with a controller, a service, a repository, and an entity.
prefix: Inside, every module uses the one layout every Spring developer knows: layered, with a controller, a service, a repository, and an entity.

text: We chose contract first: an OpenAPI file comes before any code, Gradle generates the interfaces and models, and the code must implement them, so it never drifts from what clients were promised.
prefix: We chose contract first: an OpenAPI file comes before any code, Gradle generates the interfaces and models, and the code must implement them, so it never drifts from what clients were promised.

text: The same contract generates a client interface too: one module calls another through it inside the app today, and over HTTP the day that module becomes its own service.
prefix: The same contract generates a client interface too: one module calls another through it inside the app today, and over HTTP the day that module becomes its own service.

text: Shared pieces, the error format, security, persistence, crypto, Vault, observability, and every contract, live in their own platform repository, as one Gradle build of libraries.
prefix: Shared pieces, the error format, security, persistence, crypto, Vault, observability, and every contract, live in their own platform repository, as one Gradle build of libraries.

text: The app and each adapter include that repository's build, a Gradle composite build, so the libraries are built from source and nothing is published.
prefix: The app and each adapter include that repository's build, a Gradle composite build, so the libraries are built from source and nothing is published.

text: One version catalog in the platform pins every version, and the app and both adapters read that same file.
prefix: One version catalog in the platform pins every version, and the app and both adapters read that same file.

text: Errors follow one format, R F C ninety-four fifty-seven problem details: each module lists its errors once, and every failure answers with a stable code, the request's id, and a message in English, Russian or Uzbek.
prefix: Errors follow one format, R F C ninety-four fifty-seven problem details: each module lists its errors once, and every failure answers with a stable code, the request's id, and a message in English, Russian or Uzbek.

text: Services that do one job live outside the app, each with its own contract and client: the card scheme adapters.
prefix: Services that do one job live outside the app, each with its own contract and client: the card scheme adapters.

text: One infrastructure repository starts all of it with one Docker Compose command, and each piece is explained in the episode that first uses it.
prefix: One infrastructure repository starts all of it with one Docker Compose command, and each piece is explained in the episode that first uses it.

text: Every secret, from each module's database password to the card keys, comes from Vault at startup, and the app does not start without it.
